claims.text: Grants are available for works-in-progress in fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and script projects.
The grants can cover research, travel, and other general expenditure.
Applicants are automatically considered for specific named awards, including the Eric Ambler, Taner Baybars, John Brooks, Antonia Fraser, Arthur Welton, and Great Britain Sasakawa awards.
The Authors’ Foundation fund is open to writers who have been previously published or have a contract for their project with a commercial UK publisher or producer.

For book projects, applicants must be commissioned by a commercial UK or Irish publisher for a full-length work of fiction, poetry, or non-fiction and need funding for research, travel, or other general expenditure.

Alternatively, for book projects, applicants without a publisher contract must have had at least one book published commercially by a UK or Irish publisher as the sole author or translator, with a strong likelihood of their next book being published in the UK or Ireland.
In both book project cases, authors must have a non-contributory contract where they do not pay publication costs.

For script projects, applicants must have had a work professionally performed on stage, screen, or radio in the UK or Ireland as the sole author, or be under contract to write a script for professional performance in the UK or Ireland.
Hybrid and self-published books are not eligible.
Grants cannot be awarded to cover publication, promotion, or production costs.
Grants cannot fund student tuition fees.
Grants are only awarded for one work-in-progress.
Editors are not eligible.
Applications for AI generated works are not accepted.
No author may apply to the same assessor panel twice.
Applicants who have previously received a K Blundell Trust Award or Authors’ Foundation grant must wait four years before re-applying.
There are no deadlines for this fund as it accepts submissions on a rolling basis.
Applications should be submitted via email to grants@societyofauthors.org.
Grants are usually between £2,000-£3,000.
The Eric Ambler Award is for a spy novel or thriller.
The Taner Baybars Award offers funding for original fiction in the fields of science fiction, fantasy, and magic realism (for both adult and children’s fiction).
The John Brooks Award offers funding to writers based in the West Country or Wales.
The Antonia Fraser Grant is for a biography of a woman or women.
The Arthur Welton Award is generally awarded to poets.
The Great Britain Sasakawa Grant is for works of fiction or non-fiction about any aspect of Japanese culture or society, or set in a Japanese context.
Preference for the Great Britain Sasakawa Grant will be given to works which help to interpret modern Japan to the English-speaking world.
One grant of £2,000 is awarded annually for the Great Britain Sasakawa Grant.
